title: fix: verify volume mountpoint before incrementing mount count
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->
    When MountCount is positive, mount() assumes the volume is still mounted
    and increments the count. If the mount has disappeared while the stored
    count remains stale, this can make Podman treat an unmounted volume as
    mounted.

    For filesystem-backed volumes, check the configured mountpoint before
    incrementing the count. Return an error if the check fails or the volume
    is no longer mounted.

```
root@mynuc:/tmp# podman volume create --opt type=none --opt o=bind --opt device=/tmp/d0 d0
d0

root@mynuc:/tmp# podman volume mount d0
/var/lib/containers/storage/volumes/d0/_data

root@mynuc:/home/pi# podman volume inspect d0
[
     {
          "Name": "d0",
          "Driver": "local",
          "Mountpoint": "/var/lib/containers/storage/volumes/d0/_data",
          "CreatedAt": "2026-10-06T22:22:06.685908758+08:00",
          "Labels": {},
          "Scope": "local",
          "Options": {
               "device": "/tmp/d0",
               "o": "bind",
               "type": "none"
          },
          "MountCount": 1,
          "NeedsCopyUp": true,
          "NeedsChown": true,
          "LockNumber": 0
     }
]

root@mynuc:/home/pi# umount -l /var/lib/containers/storage/volumes/d0/_data
```
```
# bleow (after patching) shall not ignore the mountpoint check silently. i think the correct path is reporting the error 
root@mynuc:/home/pi# podman run --rm --network none -v d0:/data -it busybox:1.37 sh
Error: mounting volume d0 for container a5ae003ed50deb3aefc859a3cc944d5cc34f3fcc43f0517e646f0ba4b2e9e6ae: volume d0 has mount count 1 but is not mounted
root@mynuc:/home/pi# podman volume mount d0
Error: volume d0 has mount count 1 but is not mounted
```

comments.body: I don't know if this is worth the performance penalty to handle situations where Podman mounts are being manually edited outside of our control?

> I don't know if this is worth the performance penalty to handle situations where Podman mounts are being manually edited outside of our control?

here is why I think we need this fix, which is tied to 51347e141c0bb4efe1a408cbebc414b7909f69bc . After our environment ran out of disk space, the mount point for the PG container's volume got unmounted on its own (no one did it manually). The PG container then went into a continuous restart loop, since the MountCount is 1, podman does not mount the volume again, but the mount point itself was actually empty.
i dont like the commit message. i would prefer a written commit message that explains what and why you  fixed something.  please read our guidelines for this if you have questions.
you need to add a test

If you feel this patch is worth pursuing, I'd be happy to add the tests as soon as possible, or cooperate with anyone familiar with the codebase to wrap this up. Alternatively, if you think this fix isn't necessary, feel free to close the PR.
